correctness.rationale: For each fixed compact C^3 positively curved strictly convex curve, the midpoint of independent boundary endpoints is on the boundary only at coincident endpoints. Uniform compactness localizes exceptional midpoint depths to |h|=O(sqrt(epsilon)); Frenet expansion and tubular signed distance give D(s,h)=kappa(s)h^2/8+o(h^2) uniformly. The unit-Jacobian midpoint and signed-gap chart, followed by h=sqrt(8epsilon/kappa(s))*z, yields dominated L1 convergence of the conditional densities, establishing 4sqrt(2)J, TV of location/gap marks, and weak Beta(1/2,1) exact-depth limit. Cauchy-Schwarz and total curvature prove unique curvature-square-root density and disk optimum; shrinking-axis ellipses yield the unbounded sharp range. Exact circle formula and two elliptical sampling models checked via embedded standalone code; simulations are diagnostic, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The midpoint is the natural location statistic of a chord formed by independent boundary samples. Its rare proximity to a smooth oval has a curvature-sensitive leading probability and a fully identified conditional location-and-gap law. The theorem answers a motivated sampling-design problem: among all endpoint densities it uniquely minimizes boundary-concentrated midpoints by f proportional to the square root of curvature. Unlike only computing a leading coefficient, it proves a rigid sharp fixed-perimeter disk bound and unbounded range of uniform-sampling coefficients, locating exactly how curvature dispersion affects the statistic; this is not merely a renamed short-chord integral.
